title: The EV Tax Credit Ended. Here's What Americans Did Next #shorts

scenes.text: When America's seventy-five hundred dollar tax credit for electric cars ended, sales didn't just dip. They were cut almost in half.
In September 2025, about eleven percent of new car buyers went electric. One month later, just five point eight percent.
So what did people buy instead? Hybrids. Their sales jumped almost twenty-seven percent in a year.
And used electric cars boomed. Over forty-seven thousand sold in a single month, up twenty-one percent.
Why? A new electric car still costs about fifty-six thousand dollars on average.
Sales are slowly climbing back, to about six point four percent. So did Americans reject electric cars, or just the price? Follow EV Drive.
